options: A scheduled email containing one report
A single new chart type not available in Report Designer
A replacement for Performance Analytics
A container page that arranges multiple existing reports and/or PA widgets on one or more tabs
questions.explain: A dashboard generates no new data itself — it's a canvas that arranges content (reports, PA widgets) that already exists.

questions.q: What must happen before you can add a widget to a dashboard?
options: Nothing — dashboards generate their own charts automatically
A collector job must run inside the Dashboard application
The individual report or PA widget must already exist, built in Report Designer or PA, before it can be placed on the canvas
The dashboard must first be deleted and recreated
questions.explain: The relationship is sequential: build the report or indicator widget first, then open the Dashboard application to place it on a canvas.

questions.q: Which setting matters most for a dashboard meant to stay open on a wall monitor all day, showing current data?
options: Report type
Refresh interval
Role-based visibility
Group-by field
questions.explain: Refresh interval controls how often the dashboard automatically re-pulls data for its widgets, which is essential for a live operational display.

questions.q: Why is role-based visibility described as a core design decision rather than a minor afterthought?
options: Because it has no real effect on who can open a dashboard
Because it's the setting that keeps the right data in front of the right audience, the same way a report's filter condition shapes what data appears at all
Because every dashboard in ServiceNow is public by default with no way to restrict it
Because visibility settings only apply to Performance Analytics, never to dashboards
questions.explain: A dashboard built for a Service Desk Manager showing team performance isn't something every end user should see — visibility should be set at build time, not fixed later.

questions.q: What can multiple tabs on a single dashboard be used for?
options: Changing the role-based visibility of the whole dashboard
Running collector jobs faster
Grouping related widgets separately, e.g. an Incidents tab and a Changes tab on the same dashboard
Nothing — a dashboard can only ever have one tab
questions.explain: Tabs let a single dashboard organize related widgets into separate groupings without needing a separate dashboard for each.
